report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of graph_brief.py (lines 121-206) containing file_symbols, _deep_only_modules, _tail_matches, and _neighbourhood.
risks: _tail_matches | medium | Suffix matching on dotted names may over-match, potentially mislabeling edges. | Review if over-matching is acceptable or if stricter matching is needed.
file_symbols | low | Uses ast.Name for base class identification, which may miss complex bases like function calls. | Check if complex base classes need handling.
_deep_only_modules | low | The function assumes module is None when level > 0 for relative imports, which is correct for ast.ImportFrom. | Verify with actual relative imports.

symbols.name: file_symbols
symbols.note: Top-level API: returns list of declaration lines (signatures) for a Python file.

symbols.name: _deep_only_modules
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of module names imported only inside function bodies.

symbols.name: _tail_matches
symbols.note: Checks if a dotted set plausibly denotes a relative path (suffix matching).

symbols.name: _neighbourhood
symbols.note: Returns list of nodes within given hops from targets using forward and reverse edges.

claims.text: Signatures rather than bare names, because the measured failure was not only "the module does not exist" but "the module does not define that": a name without its shape still lets a caller invent the arguments.
claims.why: The function returns signatures (via _sig) rather than bare names, as shown in the code.

claims.text: Methods are included one level down for classes, since Shift.tick() is the kind of thing a caller needs and the class name alone does not give it.
claims.why: The code iterates over class body and adds indented signatures for methods (lines 153-157).

claims.text: Deeper nesting is deliberately not listed -- it is not API.
claims.why: The code only processes one level of class body (node.body), not deeper nesting.

claims.text: Computed here rather than read from the index because the index publishes a flat edge list with no depth: it correctly INCLUDES function-body edges (12 edges for offload.py against 7 top-level import statements -- verified), it just cannot say which ones they are.
claims.why: The claim references 'offload.py' and 'the index' which are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: One extra AST pass over a handful of neighbour files buys the distinction.
claims.why: The claim refers to 'neighbour files' which are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Suffix matching on the dotted path, because a function-body import may be written from .kairos import drafts or import daedalus.kairos.drafts and both denote daedalus/kairos/drafts.py.
claims.why: The function uses suffix matching on the dotted name, splitting on '.' and checking last one or two segments.

claims.text: Over-matching here only ever adds a * mark to an edge that is genuinely present, so a wrong guess mislabels a true edge rather than inventing one.
claims.why: The claim refers to a '*' mark and edge labeling which are not present in this chunk.

observations.what: file_symbols returns signatures including arguments for functions and methods.
_deep_only_modules computes top-level and deep imports, returning deep - top.
_tail_matches uses suffix matching on dotted names to check if a relative path is plausible.
_neighbourhood is declared but its body is incomplete (ends mid-line).
In file_symbols, base class identification uses ast.Name only, ignoring other expressions.
In _deep_only_modules, for ast.ImportFrom, module is None when level > 0; the code correctly returns [] in that case.
